references.text: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is most holy among the Lord's fire offerings.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy among the Lord's fire offerings.
Instructions that the grain offering must be eaten unleavened by Aaron and his sons in a holy place, because it is most holy.
The grain offering shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting.
The grain offering baked in an oven or cooked on a pan belongs to the priest who presents it.
The priest may eat from his God's food, both from what is most holy and from what is holy.
The most holy offerings belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall be eaten in a holy place.
Unleavened bread and unleavened cakes as part of the ordination offering for the priests.
Context: Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord's presence, so Moses spoke to the surviving sons.
The priests shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
